\textbf{Cross-cohort replication check.} (a) Stratified enrichment (observed over TF-stratified expected perturbation positives among promoted evaluable edges) per study and universe (global universe primary, tissue universes secondary), with 95\% TF-bootstrap intervals where at least 5 TFs contribute (post hoc rule); intervals reaching 0 are cut at the axis. Marker shape gives the power class locked before any replication outcome was computed (filled: adequately powered; open: below the support floor); the endpoint-unattainable class (X; the positive-rate margins cannot reach the endpoint) was added post hoc; dashed line: endpoint 1.5 (non-evaluable studies omitted). Global universe: Dixit 2016: 0 observed vs 0.2 expected promoted positives (power 0.03, MDE 27.4); Norman 2019 1.95 [1.64, 2.45] (power 1.00, MDE 1.39); Papalexi 2021 2.24 [1.72, 4.86] (power 1.00, MDE 1.41); Replogle 2022 1.57 [1.12, 4.86] (power 0.99, MDE 1.56). Pass rate 3/4 evaluable studies (a study below the support floor is reported as underpowered but counts as not passing) and 3/3 adequately powered studies. (b) Minimum detectable enrichment at 80\% power and one-sided $\alpha=0.05$ from the design alone (dotted: design enrichment 2). (c) Pooled within-TF odds ratio $e^{\mu}$ and the predicted odds ratio of a new study in the Bayesian random-effects model under the primary and 7 alternative prior specifications and a model with a TF-level random slope$^{\dagger}$ (median and 95\% credible interval; N, normal; HN, half-normal; $^{\dagger}$post hoc). Primary prior: 2.82 [1.42, 4.09], $P(e^{\mu}\geq 1.5)=0.97$; sceptical prior $\mu\sim N(0,0.2^2)$: 1.21 [0.81, 1.81], $P=0.15$; across the alternative priors $P(e^{\mu}\geq 1.5)$ ranges from 0.15 to 0.99; TF random slope: 3.28 [1.71, 5.42], $P=0.99$.
